question: Our website was built by an agency last year. Since this morning the homepage just says the site is having technical problems. I read that WordPress emails someone a special login link when this happens, but nobody on our team got anything. Who is that email sent to, and how do we get back in without it?

facts.fact: Recovery mode emails are sent to the Administration Email Address set in Settings > General.
facts.evidence: Recovery mode and critical error notifications are sent to this address.

facts.fact: Without the email, plugins can be temporarily deactivated by renaming their folders via FTP or the host's file manager.
facts.evidence: If you’re comfortable using FTP (or, if it’s available with your web host — an online file handler) you may temporarily deactivate one or several plugins by renaming their folder names.

question: I clicked update in the dashboard and now the whole site only shows a line saying it's down for maintenance and to check back in a minute. That was two hours ago. How do I get my site back?

facts.fact: Delete the .maintenance file to remove the message.
facts.evidence: To stop that message from being displayed to vistors, just delete the .maintenance file.

facts.fact: The .maintenance file is in the WordPress base folder, the one that contains wp-admin.
facts.evidence: As part of the automatic upgrade WordPress places a file named .maintenance in the blog base folder (folder that contains the wp-admin folder).

question: I changed my link format so post addresses show the post title instead of ?p=123. Now the home page loads but every single post gives a page not found error. What went wrong?

facts.fact: 404s with pretty permalinks can be caused by the Apache mod_rewrite module not being enabled; the host may need to activate it.
facts.evidence: Note: you may have to ask your host to activate mod_rewrite.

facts.fact: If .htaccess isn't writable, WordPress shows rewrite rules that must be copied manually into the .htaccess file.
facts.evidence: You need to manually copy everything in this text box into your .htaccess file to make your new Permalinks work.

question: People signing up on our community site say the password email never arrives, even though the site says it was sent. We host WordPress ourselves on a machine in our office rather than with a hosting company. Any idea why?

facts.fact: WordPress sends mail through PHP's mail() function, which relies on sendmail.
facts.evidence: WordPress uses the standard PHP mail() function, which uses sendmail.

facts.fact: On your own server without an SMTP/mail server set up, the email will never be sent.
facts.evidence: This is not generally a problem if you are using a hosting service, but if you are using your own box and do not have an SMTP server, the mail will never send.

question: How do I set up shipping zones in WooCommerce so customers in my town get free delivery and everyone else pays a flat rate?
I updated the text on my homepage and saved it, but when I look at the site it still shows the old version. My host sells it as a managed WordPress plan, if that matters.

facts.fact: Clear the browser cache, since the browser may be showing a stored copy of the page.
facts.evidence: The solution in this case is to clear or empty your browser’s cache.

facts.fact: Managed WordPress hosting often uses server-side caching; look for an option to flush that cache.
facts.evidence: If you are using a managed WordPress service from your hosting provider and you are seeing this issue, you may want to see if they have an option to manually flush the cache.

question: I followed a tutorial and pasted a bit of code into a paragraph to make the text pink. Now that paragraph shows an error box in the editor instead of my text. What are my options to fix it, and can I keep the pink?

facts.fact: The paragraph block doesn't expect inline style attributes, so it flags the content as an error.
facts.evidence: Style attributes aren’t expected by the block, so it will return an error.

facts.fact: Attempt Block Recovery restores the block but removes the custom code.
facts.evidence: This option will automatically remove the custom code and revert the block back to its previous safe state.

facts.fact: Converting to a Custom HTML block keeps the HTML customization (e.g. the pink color).
facts.evidence: This will convert the invalid content directly into an HTML block and keep any HTML customization made.

question: My laptop died halfway through writing a long blog post and I hadn't hit save. Is all of that gone? Also, does WordPress fill up the database by saving a copy every minute?

facts.fact: Autosaves are kept as a special revision; when you reopen the post WordPress warns you a backup exists and offers a link to restore it.
facts.evidence: Autosaves are stored as a special type of revision; they do not overwrite the actual post.

facts.fact: Only one autosave per user per post is kept; new autosaves overwrite old ones.
facts.evidence: There is only ever a maximum of one autosave per user for any given post.

question: An SEO guy told me I should block a bunch of folders and scripts in my robots file to rank better. Is that actually a good idea?

facts.fact: Adding robots.txt entries to help SEO is a misconception.
facts.evidence: Adding entries to robots.txt to help SEO is popular misconception.

facts.fact: Use page-level noindex tags instead of robots.txt blocking for low-quality parts of the site.
facts.evidence: Use page-level noindex tags instead, to tackle low-quality parts of your site.

facts.fact: Google advises against blocking JS and CSS files.
facts.evidence: Since 2009, Google has been evermore vocal in its advice to avoid blocking JS & CSS files

question: When I click to edit my homepage with Elementor it just shows a spinning loader forever. How do I fix that?

Ticket from a client: their developer made a custom user role for the marketing person so she can work on the site's templates. She can open the Site Editor, but the template sections won't load and nothing saves. What should I check?

facts.fact: Template and template-part endpoints require the edit_theme_options capability.
facts.evidence: For template and template-part endpoints, WordPress checks whether the current user has the edit_theme_options capability.

facts.fact: Check the browser developer tools for REST API requests returning 401 or 403 to find the missing capability.
facts.evidence: If a custom role can open the Site Editor but some sections fail to load or save, check the browser’s developer tools for REST API requests returning 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden responses.

facts.fact: Other capabilities such as edit_posts, edit_pages and edit_others_posts may also be needed.
facts.evidence: For example, users may also need edit_posts, edit_pages, and edit_others_posts to fully utilize the Site Editor’s features.

question: I want to let customers create their own accounts on my shop's site. I'm nervous though: what will a brand new account be allowed to do? I don't want strangers writing posts.

facts.fact: Self-registration is turned on with the 'Anyone can register' option in Settings > General.
facts.evidence: Anyone can register – Check this checkbox if you want anyone to be able to register an account on your site.

facts.fact: New accounts get the New User Default Role chosen in Settings > General.
facts.evidence: This Default Role will be assigned to newly registered members or users added via the Administration > Users > Users Screen.

facts.fact: If that role is Subscriber, the user can only manage their own profile.
facts.evidence: Subscriber (slug: ‘subscriber’) – somebody who can only manage their profile.

question: I already run one WordPress site and my cheap hosting plan only gives me one database. Can I put a second WordPress site in that same database, or do I need to upgrade?

facts.fact: A separate database per WordPress installation is not required.
facts.evidence: It is not essential to create a new database for each WordPress installation.

facts.fact: When sharing a database, each installation needs a unique table prefix set in wp-config.php.
facts.evidence: If you are using the same database for multiple WordPress installations, take care to edit the wp-config.php file ensuring that each installation has a unique database prefix.

question: My home page is a welcome page and my articles live on a separate page called News. I gave the News page a password and a special page template, but visitors aren't asked for any password and the template isn't used. Why?

facts.fact: The page chosen as the Posts page doesn't prompt for a password even if it is password protected.
facts.evidence: Even if the selected Page is password protected, visitors will NOT be prompted for a password when viewing the Posts Page.

facts.fact: Any template assigned to the Posts page is ignored; the theme's index.php (or home.php) controls it.
facts.evidence: Also, any Template assigned to the Page will be ignored and the theme’s index.php (or home.php if it exists) will control the display of the posts.

question: I want my site in both Spanish and English, with a little flag switcher so visitors can pick. Should I use WPML or Polylang, and how do I set it up?

I have members-only pages for different clients, each with its own password. A client who has access to two of them complains she has to keep re-typing passwords when going back and forth. Can I fix that?

facts.fact: WordPress only remembers one post password at a time in the browser cookie.
facts.evidence: WordPress will only track one password at a time.

facts.fact: If several posts share the same password, the reader only enters it once to access all of them.
facts.evidence: Furthermore, if multiple posts use the same password, the reader will only have to enter the password once to access every post (see caveat below).

question: Our writers say they never get an email when someone comments on their articles and the comment is waiting for approval. Only I seem to get those emails. Is something misconfigured?

facts.fact: Held-for-moderation notifications go to the site's administration email address.
facts.evidence: When this setting is enabled, the notification is sent to the site’s administration email address, as configured under Settings > General.

facts.fact: Post authors only get the notification if they can edit comments and have at least the Editor role.
facts.evidence: If the post author has permission to edit comments and holds at least an Editor role, they will also receive the notification.

facts.fact: Users with the default Author role don't have moderation rights and get no notification.
facts.evidence: Post authors with the default Author role do not have comment moderation rights and will not receive a notification email.

question: To stop rude comments I added "ass" to the list of words that get comments thrown out. Now a customer says her comment asking about our class times vanished, and I can't find it anywhere, not even in pending. What happened?

facts.fact: Blocked words match inside other words (e.g. 'press' matches 'WordPress'), so 'class' matched.
facts.evidence: It will match inside words, so “press” will match “WordPress”

facts.fact: Comments matching the disallowed keys are deleted immediately without notification, so genuine comments can be lost.
facts.evidence: Genuine comments could be deleted without you ever knowing they were there.

question: I switched off comments in the settings but my older blog posts are still getting new comments. How do I turn them off on all those old posts without opening each one?

facts.fact: Turning off comments in Settings > Discussion usually only affects future content.
facts.evidence: Disabling comments in Settings > Discussion usually applies only to future content.

facts.fact: Use Bulk actions > Edit on the Posts screen and set Comments to 'Do not allow'.
facts.evidence: In the bulk edit interface, set Comments to Do not allow.

question: Where do I paste my Google Analytics tracking code so I can see how many people visit?
what's a good admin password? i was going to use my dog's name and the year i was born

facts.fact: Use at least 20 characters.
facts.evidence: You shouldn’t pick a password containing less than 20 characters.

facts.fact: Avoid personal information like pet names or birth year because of social engineering risk.
facts.evidence: All these items are personal (mostly public) information and thus possible risks for social engineering.

facts.fact: Mix uppercase/lowercase letters, numbers and special characters (or use the built-in generated password).
facts.evidence: These strong passwords contain 24 characters, numbers, letters, capitals, and special characters.

question: I can't remember my login and the reset link email never shows up. I do have access to the database tool in my hosting panel (phpMyAdmin). Can I change the password from there?

facts.fact: In the wp_users table, edit your user and replace the value in user_pass with the new password.
facts.evidence: Next to the user_pass is a long list of numbers and letters.

facts.fact: Select MD5 from the function dropdown before saving.
facts.evidence: Once you have done that, click the dropdown menu indicated, and select MD5 from the menu.

question: I know my password is right, but every time I log in I just land back on the login screen. What can I try?

facts.fact: Make sure cookies are enabled by clearing browser cookies and cache.
facts.evidence: In order to make sure that cookies are enabled for your browser, you need to:

facts.fact: Some firewalls block WordPress logins; disable the firewall and try again.
facts.evidence: Some firewalls (e.g., eTrust Personal Firewall) block you from logging in to WordPress.

facts.fact: Username and password are case-sensitive.
facts.evidence: Remember: the Username and Password fields are case-sensitive.

question: Google is warning visitors away from my site and there are weird pharmacy links on my pages. I already changed my WordPress admin password. Is that enough? I'm worried whoever did it is still logged in.

facts.fact: Change credentials for every access point: FTP/SFTP, wp-admin, the hosting control panel and MySQL.
facts.evidence: When we say access points we mean things like FTP / SFTP, WP-ADMIN, CPANEL (or any other administrator panel you use with your host) and MYSQL.

facts.fact: Replace the secret keys in wp-config.php to force everyone currently logged in to be logged out.
facts.evidence: You also want to clear any users that might be actively logged into WordPress.

facts.fact: Change the passwords again once the site has been cleaned.
facts.evidence: So if you only changed them when you discovered the hack, change them again now.

question: Can I write a post today and have it go live automatically next Monday at 8am?
Months ago I switched on automatic updates for all my plugins, but they never update on their own; I still end up doing it by hand. What could be stopping them?

facts.fact: Plugin auto-updates depend on WordPress cron tasks, which may not run correctly on some servers/setups.
facts.evidence: Indeed, they rely on WordPress Cron tasks to actually perform the update.

facts.fact: Check Tools > Site Health for error messages about cron.
facts.evidence: To check if WordPress Cron tasks are running correctly, go to Tools > Site Health and search for any error message.

facts.fact: A failing loopback request (reported in Site Health) can break scheduled events.
facts.evidence: Loopback requests are used to run scheduled events and are also used by the built-in editors for themes and plugins to verify code stability.

question: Our old developer added something that runs on every page, but it isn't in my Plugins list so there's no deactivate button. How do I switch it off?

facts.fact: It is likely a must-use plugin; these are hidden from the normal Plugins list and can only be disabled by removing the file from wp-content/mu-plugins.
facts.evidence: Must-use plugins do not show in the default list of plugins on the Plugins page and cannot be disabled except by removing the plugin file from the must-use directory, which is found in wp-content/mu-plugins by default.

question: I'm moving my blog to a new hosting company and starting with a fresh WordPress install there. How do I bring my posts and comments over?

facts.fact: Use Tools > Export to download an XML (WXR) export file.
facts.evidence: When you click the Download Export File button, WordPress will create an XML file for you to save to your computer.

facts.fact: On the new site, import it via Tools > Import > WordPress.
facts.evidence: Once you’ve saved the download file, you can use Administration > Tools > Import > WordPress at another WordPress site to import this data

question: A former member asked us to delete everything we have about her. If I do it in WordPress, can I undo it if it was a mistake? And what about our nightly backups?

facts.fact: Confirmed erasure requests cannot be reversed.
facts.evidence: Erasure requests cannot be reversed after they have been confirmed.

facts.fact: The tool doesn't remove data from backups; be careful when restoring from backups so the erasure is respected.
facts.evidence: When restoring an archived copy of your site, your requests for erasure should be respected.

question: How do I connect my Mailchimp list so people who fill in the newsletter box on my site get added automatically?
Chrome shows "not secure" next to my site address. Does it actually matter for a small bakery website? I'm worried the padlock thing will slow the site down.

facts.fact: HTTPS actually makes the site faster for almost all visitors.
facts.evidence: As a result, HTTPS will actually make your site faster for almost all visitors.

facts.fact: Search engines penalize sites without HTTPS.
facts.evidence: Many search engines will add a penalty to web sites that don’t use HTTPS, thus making it harder to reach the best spots in search results.

question: My recipes are filed under two categories, like Desserts and Vegan, and the web address always shows the wrong one. Can I control which one appears in the link?

facts.fact: Only one category can appear in the permalink.
facts.evidence: When you assign multiple categories to a post, only one can show up in the permalink.

facts.fact: The category shown is chosen alphabetically.
facts.evidence: Which category gets displayed in the permalink is determined alphabetically.

facts.fact: A plugin is needed to choose which category is shown.
facts.evidence: If you want to choose which category shows up in the permalink, you can use one of the plugins from the plugin directory.
